audit_headline: Watson Plumbing has no phone number on its Google Business Profile, which means potential customers searching for a plumber in Macon cannot call you directly from Google Search or Maps.
summary: Watson Plumbing & Associates LLC has a solid 4.0-star rating from 70 reviews and a strong reputation for responsiveness and fair pricing based on recent review themes. However, the profile is missing three critical contact elements: no phone number is listed, no website is linked, and no hours are posted. These gaps make it significantly harder for searchers to reach you or confirm you're available, even though your reviews show you respond quickly.

sections.title: Google Business Profile
sections.summary: Your profile is set to Plumber and shows 10 or more photos, but it's missing the three most important contact signals: phone, hours, and website.

findings.observation: No phone number is listed on the profile. When someone searches 'plumber near me' or 'emergency plumber Macon GA' and finds your business, they see no way to call you directly from the search result or map listing.
findings.recommendation: Add your business phone number to the profile immediately. This is the single most important fix for a service business.

findings.observation: No hours are posted. Searchers cannot see when you're open, which creates uncertainty about whether you're available now or if they should call.
findings.recommendation: Add your operating hours, including any after-hours or emergency availability if you offer it. If hours vary or you're on-call, post your standard office hours and note emergency service in the business description.

findings.observation: No website is linked. The profile offers no way for a searcher to learn more about your services, see pricing context, or contact you online.
findings.recommendation: If you have a website, link it in the profile. If you don't have one, consider at minimum a simple one-page site with your services, contact info, and service area, or use a free Google Site as a placeholder.

findings.observation: Your primary category is correctly set to Plumber, which matches your business type and helps Google surface you for plumbing searches in Macon.
The profile shows 10 or more photos, which is a floor — the API caps visibility at 10, so you may have more. Photos help searchers recognize your trucks, team, and work quality.

sections.title: Reviews & Reputation
sections.summary: You have a 4.0-star rating from 70 reviews, which is a solid foundation. Recent reviews consistently mention responsiveness, fair pricing, and professionalism, though the most recent visible review is from a year ago.

findings.observation: Your 70 reviews give you meaningful volume for a local plumber, and the 4.0-star rating is strong. Four of the five most recent reviews are 5-star and highlight quick response times — one mentions you 'showed up the day after Christmas' for a sewer backup, and another notes you came 'a day before they thought they could originally get to it.'

The most recent review visible in the data is from a year ago. If you've received reviews more recently, they're not surfacing here; if not, a year without fresh reviews can signal to searchers that your business may be less active.
findings.recommendation: Ask recent customers for reviews. A steady trickle of new reviews — even one or two per month — keeps your profile current and reinforces trust.

findings.observation: One of the five recent reviews is 1-star and mentions a pool water delivery service and 'unprofessionalism' from office staff. This review describes a service (pool water delivery) that doesn't align with your Plumber category, which may confuse searchers about what you actually do.
findings.recommendation: If pool water delivery is not a core service, consider clarifying your service offerings in your business description so searchers understand your focus is plumbing and septic work.

findings.observation: The Google Places API does not reveal whether you've responded to reviews. Responding to reviews — especially negative ones — is a recognized trust signal and shows engagement.
findings.recommendation: Log into your Google Business Profile and check if you've replied to your reviews, particularly the 1-star review about pool water. If not, reply professionally and briefly. Make it a habit to respond to new reviews within a few days.

sections.title: Website & Online Presence
sections.summary: No website is linked on your profile, so this audit could not evaluate your site's local-search signals.

findings.observation: No website is linked on the Google Business Profile. This means searchers who want to learn more about your services, see a full service list, check service-area coverage, or contact you online have no path to do so from your profile.
findings.recommendation: If you have a website, add the URL to your profile under 'Edit profile -> Website.' If you don't have one, consider building a simple one-page site with your services, contact info, and service area — even a free Google Site or basic WordPress page is better than nothing.

findings.observation: Because no website is linked, this audit could not check for local-search signals like a homepage title that includes 'Plumber' and 'Macon GA,' click-to-call phone links, HTTPS, mobile-friendliness, or LocalBusiness structured data.
findings.recommendation: Once you link a website, revisit these elements. A homepage title like 'Watson Plumbing – Licensed Plumber in Macon, GA' and a prominent click-to-call button are quick wins for local relevance and conversion.

sections.title: Call Handling & Availability
sections.summary: With no phone number on the profile and no hours posted, searchers have no way to call you or know when you're available.

findings.observation: No phone number is listed on the profile, which means Google Search and Maps results show no call button. Your reviews mention quick response and emergency availability, but searchers can't act on that without a number to dial.
findings.recommendation: Add your phone number to the profile. This is the most direct path for a searcher to become a caller.

findings.observation: No hours are posted, so searchers don't know if you're open now, if you offer evening or weekend service, or if you handle after-hours emergencies. One review mentions you responded 'the day after Christmas,' which suggests you may offer emergency service, but that's invisible to new searchers.
findings.recommendation: Post your hours. If you offer 24/7 emergency service, note that in your business description and consider setting hours to reflect on-call availability or standard office hours with a note about emergency dispatch.

fix_list.action: Add your business phone number to the Google Business Profile.
fix_list.rationale: No phone number is listed, which means searchers cannot call you from Google Search or Maps. Your reviews show you respond quickly, but without a number, that responsiveness is invisible. This is the highest-impact fix for a service business.
fix_list.where: Google Business Profile -> Edit profile -> Contact -> Phone

fix_list.action: Post your operating hours on the profile.
fix_list.rationale: No hours are posted, so searchers don't know when you're available. One review mentions you responded on a holiday, which suggests flexibility, but new customers can't see that. Posting hours reduces uncertainty and can surface your business in 'open now' searches.
fix_list.where: Google Business Profile -> Edit profile -> Hours

fix_list.action: Link your website to the profile, or create a simple one-page site if you don't have one.
fix_list.rationale: No website is linked, so searchers who want more detail about your services, pricing context, or service area have no path. A website also allows you to add local-search signals like a city-specific homepage title and click-to-call links.
fix_list.where: Google Business Profile -> Edit profile -> Website. If you need to build a site, consider a free Google Site or a basic WordPress page with services, contact info, and service area.

fix_list.action: Check if you've responded to your reviews, and reply to any you've missed — especially the 1-star review about pool water delivery.
fix_list.rationale: The API does not show whether you've replied to reviews. Responding to reviews, particularly negative ones, is a recognized trust signal. The 1-star review mentions a service (pool water) that may not be your focus; a brief, professional reply can clarify your core services.
fix_list.where: Google Business Profile -> Reviews -> Click on a review -> Reply

fix_list.action: Ask recent customers for Google reviews to bring your review recency up to date.
fix_list.rationale: Your most recent visible review is from a year ago. Fresh reviews signal that your business is active and help maintain trust. Your 70 reviews are a strong base; a few new ones per month keep momentum.
fix_list.where: After completing a job, send a follow-up text or email with a direct link to your Google review page (find it at Google Business Profile -> Home -> 'Get more reviews').

fix_list.action: Add a business description that highlights your core plumbing and septic services and mentions emergency availability if you offer it.
fix_list.rationale: One recent review mentions pool water delivery, which may confuse searchers about your focus. A clear description that emphasizes plumbing, sewer line work, and septic systems (themes from your positive reviews) helps searchers understand what you do. Mentioning emergency service ties to your 'day after Christmas' responsiveness.
fix_list.where: Google Business Profile -> Edit profile -> Business description

fix_list.action: Once you link a website, ensure the homepage title includes 'Plumber' and 'Macon GA' and add a prominent click-to-call button.
fix_list.rationale: A homepage title like 'Watson Plumbing – Licensed Plumber in Macon, GA' is a known local-search relevance signal. A click-to-call button (a tel: link) makes it easy for mobile visitors to dial you immediately, which is critical for emergency plumbing searches.
fix_list.where: Your website's homepage <title> tag (ask your web developer or edit in your site builder) and homepage header or hero section for the click-to-call button.

not_checked: Whether you've responded to your Google reviews — the API does not reveal this. Log into your Google Business Profile and check the Reviews section to see if you've replied.
Your actual photo count beyond 10 — the API caps visibility at 10, so you may have more. Check your profile's Photos section to see the full count.
Whether you have a website that's simply not linked — if you do have a site, add the URL to your profile immediately.

Your call answer rate or missed-call volume — this audit has no access to phone data. Consider calling your own number after hours to test your voicemail, or set up a missed-call text-back system if you don't already have one.
Whether you offer 24/7 emergency service — your reviews suggest you respond quickly, but this isn't stated on the profile. If you do, add it to your hours or description.
closing_note: Watson Plumbing has a strong reputation and solid review themes around responsiveness and fair pricing, but your profile is missing the three most basic contact elements. Adding a phone number, hours, and a website link are quick fixes that will make it significantly easier for searchers to reach you. These are recognized local-search best practices, not guarantees, but they remove friction between a search and a call.
